context.scope: Private subprocess; owned 128MB Python Lambda, two versions, one reserved slot; SQS runtime/destination records; exact-function CloudTrail data events. No logging grants. Retry and age controls positively observed before deletion.
context.serialization: Account normalized; receipt handles and credential identity fields redacted; SDK request IDs and native timing retained. ZIP blobs base64; invocation Payload JSON decoded. Caller source IPs normalized; audit credential fields redacted. Runtime request IDs remain native and are stable across retries.
context.ordering: Observations sorted by response completion; all elapsed fields share capture_started_at origin. CloudTrail events retain delivery-document order, not execution order; delivered_object_key identifies their source.

limitations: Bounded absence is not evidence that AWS never delivers.

Unchanged target retry2/age240: ordinary failure control proves three entries and RetriesExhausted; separate 80-second-per-error control proves EventAgeExceeded before three entries. Distinct sibling age60 control retained. These establish applied settings, not exact deletion scheduling.

Runtime markers precede errors. Switch mutations follow markers by four seconds, not an independently instrumented exit signal. Each event retains the same native request ID over both runtime entries and its terminal record; deployment/version and runtime timestamps distinguish entries.
Two stable and two retarget success samples do not establish a universal approximateInvokeCount algorithm.
CloudTrail data-event delivery is asynchronous; missing events alone are not execution evidence.

cleanup_interruption.message: Connection was closed before a valid response from https://cloudtrail.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/. Function deletion and subsequent ResourceNotFoundException checkpoint were already retained. Cleanup resumed in a fresh subprocess.

metric_summary.limitations: CloudWatch publication is asynchronous; empty data is not proof of zero. Query performed after the bounded queue observation window and function deletion. Dropped totals include ordinary retry-budget and slow-age controls on this same alias.

audit_capture.note: Cleanup recovery re-fetched delivered objects. Identical event IDs from the same object are retained once here; each actual get-object request, response metadata and raw gzip digest remain in observations. This is capture re-fetch deduplication, not a claim that CloudTrail cannot deliver duplicates.

applied_controls.retry_budget: Exact target alias: three real always-failing runtime entries and terminal RetriesExhausted/count3 establish the observed retry budget. They alone do not establish age240.
applied_controls.event_age: Same unchanged target alias: two 80-second failing runtime entries and terminal EventAgeExceeded/count2 establish applied non-default age control independently of retry exhaustion. Separate age60 sibling produced one failing entry and EventAgeExceeded/count1.
applied_controls.propagation_limit: The ordinary control uses retry2, which equals the AWS default. Its purpose is a positive observed budget, not proof of a non-default retry update. The same-target slow control demonstrates non-default age behavior before deletion.

deleted_retry2.conclusion: Applied retry/age barriers exclude the earlier missing-control ambiguity, but this bounded capture still provides no positive terminal destination or terminal drop for the deleted alias. The accepted Event request ID positively correlates an initial InvokeExecution at 00:12:11Z and AWSService lambda.amazonaws.com Invoke audit events at 00:12:12Z and 00:13:08Z, the latter about 57 seconds after admission. These are service redispatch observations, not handler-entry or terminal-result evidence: requestParameters, responseElements and errorCode are absent on the service Invoke records. Initial InvokeExecution occurred while the reserved slot was positively occupied; the deleted event emitted no runtime marker. This does not establish that AWS never delivers, that the event remained pending throughout the window, or a terminal deletion timing rule.

success_count_comparison.conclusion: Success/count1 after two runtime entries occurs both without alias retargeting and with v1-to-v2 retargeting in these four samples. Thus the prior count1 observation does not require a version-change reset. Together with all-failure count3 controls, the captures distinguish observed success and failure outcomes but do not prove a universal undocumented counter algorithm.

metrics_accounting.conclusion: Received3 matches two controls plus deleted Event. Dropped2 and Invocations/Errors5 are fully accounted for by the known 3-entry retry control and 2-entry age control. There is no extra positive dropped count establishing a terminal discard of the deleted Event. Publication lag and post-deletion querying remain limitations.
